Description:
The NURBS twin of ConesTangentAtMantlePoint: two identical cones touching TANGENTIALLY at one point of
their mantles, then united, intersected and subtracted both ways. Neither mantle is a ConicalSurface -
both cones are solid.ruled between two exact nine pole NURBS circles, so both are RuledSurface and the
contact has to be found by the general search on ISurface rather than by the canal form of a quadric.

coneA is the ruled solid between the circle r = 19 at z = 0 and the circle r = 10 at z = 18. Its mantle
lies on the cone with apex (0, 0, 38) and half angle atan(1/2); the apex itself is cut away, which is
what the ruled construction needs - a NURBS circle of radius zero is not a curve.

coneB is coneA rotated by 180 degrees about the surface NORMAL of coneA at one point of its mantle:
  P = (14.25, 0, 9.5)   a point of the ruling from (19, 0, 0) towards the apex (0, 0, 38), a quarter of
                        the way up, so it is well inside the truncated part
  n = (2, 0, 1)         the outward normal there - perpendicular to the ruling (-19, 0, 38), since
                        -19*2 + 38*1 = 0, and to the circumferential direction (0, 1, 0)

Rotating about the normal at P fixes P and fixes the tangent plane at P, so coneB touches coneA at P and
both are tangent to the same plane there. That is the point of the case. A cone touches its tangent
plane along a whole ruling, so both cones touch that plane along a ruling, and the two rulings are
different lines crossing at P. The intersection curve of the two mantles therefore has a NODE at P - two
branches crossing - which is the degenerate situation a surface/surface intersection has to survive.

The angle is 180 degrees on purpose: the rotation is then an involution, coneB = f(coneA) AND
coneA = f(coneB), so the pair is symmetric and the two differences must come out equal. Under it the
base circle of coneA lands at centre (-1.9, 0, 3.8) and its top circle at (12.5, 0, -7), 18 apart as
they must be, with the axis direction (0.8, 0, -0.6).
Expected:
Both operands are the same truncated cone and coneB is a rigid image of coneA, so every measured
quantity must come out the same for both:
  volume      pi*18/3*(19^2 + 19*10 + 10^2) = 3906*pi = 12271.0609049217
  area        lateral pi*(19+10)*sqrt(18^2+9^2) = pi*29*20.1246117975 plus the two lids pi*361 and
              pi*100, together 3281.7508581065
  edgeLength  the two circles measure as their chord polygons 4*r*sqrt(2) (see
              RuledSolidsFromNurbsCircles), 107.4802307404 and 56.5685424949, plus the two seams
              2*20.1246117975: 204.2979968303
coneA reaches z from 0 to 18 and |x|, |y| <= 19; coneB is its rigid image.

The results are pinned by three exact identities, none of which needs a computed value:
  1  volume(coneUnion) + volume(coneInter) = volume(coneA) + volume(coneB) = 7812*pi = 24542.1218098434
  2  volume(coneAminusB) = 12271.0609049217 - volume(coneInter)
  3  volume(coneAminusB) = volume(coneBminusA), from the involution - the sharpest of the three

The one remaining unknown was computed independently by Monte Carlo over the bounding box of coneA,
8e6 samples, using the exact cone volume as a control variate:
  volume(coneInter)     5182.3 +- 3.7
  volume(coneUnion)     24542.1218098434 - that = 19359.8
  volume(coneAminusB)   12271.0609049217 - that =  7088.8 +- 4.1 (measured directly), same for
                        coneBminusA
So the results are checkable against real values to about a tenth of a percent, not merely captured.

WHAT MAY LEGITIMATELY VARY. How many solids each difference falls into is NOT fixed by this prose. In
ConesTangentAtMantlePoint, where the same construction is carried out on ConicalSurface, each difference
came out as two solids - a main body and a pair of lobes that meet the rest only at the tangency point,
so they are one non manifold solid and the split is right. The truncation here changes how far the
second cone reaches, so the same is likely but not guaranteed; whatever comes out has to be judged
against the volume identities above before its baseline is recorded.

WHY THESE RADII AND NOT OTHERS. A planar face whose outline is a rational NURBS circle is measured
through Border.Area -> BSpline2D.GetArea -> GeneralCurve2D.GetArea -> Approximate(false, 0.0), and for
most radii that biarc approximation degenerates into four straight lines, so the lid measures 2*r*r
instead of pi*r*r - the defect RuledSolidsFromNurbsCircles documents and pins. Measured over a range of
radii it turns out NOT to be a simple threshold: the lid is exact for r = 9.5, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 18
and 19 and short by the factor 2/pi for r = 2.5, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 20, 22 and 25. Every radius
in this case is taken from the first list, so every number below is the geometry and not a measurement
artefact. Change a radius and the case may start measuring a lid at 2/pi of its area, which looks like a
regression of the boolean operation and is none.
Status:
KNOWN FAILURE since the case was written on 2026-09-17. All four operations hit the assertion
"loops.Count should never be 0" inside BooleanOperation (call ids 11 to 14), so nothing is stored under
any of the four names.

That is the same assertion the quadric twin ConesTangentAtMantlePoint used to hit before it was fixed on
2026-08-24, on the same geometry and with the same tangential node at one point of the two mantles. The
difference is only the surface: there the mantles are ConicalSurface and the canal form solves the
contact in closed form, here they are RuledSurface. Switching the general search in
Surfaces.TangentialContacts off changes nothing - the same four calls fail with the same message - so
the contact is not what breaks; what is built from it is.

The two operands are correct and, more to the point, they measure IDENTICALLY although they are
independent objects: coneA 12271.0609105 and coneB 12271.0609099, both against the exact 3906*pi =
12271.0609049217, with the same area and the same edgeLength to the last recorded digit. They have to -
coneB is a rigid image of coneA - and that they do means the input of the case is sound and the failure
is the operation's.

When the operations start returning, the three identities in the Expected section pin the answer without
needing any measurement, and the Monte Carlo value for the intersection, 5182.3 +- 3.7, checks it
against something the code under test had no part in.

coneB.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 12271.0609099 against 12271.0609049, 4.1e-10. the rigid image of coneA, and it measures the same volume to 5e-11, the same area and the same edgeLength to the last recorded digit.
